newsitem.title: NEPAL: Three South Koreans climb Mount Dhaulagiri I.
newsitem.headline: Three South Koreans climb Mount Dhaulagiri I.

text.p: Three South Korean mountaineers scaled Mount Dhaulagiri I, the world's seventh highest mountain, last week, the Nepalese tourism ministry said on Sunday.

The three Koreans along with their Nepalese Sherpa reached the summit of the 8,167-metre (26,795-foot) peak after trekking for 12 hours and 10 minutes from their camp on the southeast ridge climbing route on April 27, the ministry said.
The leader of the expedition told Reuters before leaving for the mountains that the altitude of the camp would be about 6,300 metres (nearly 24,000 feet).
All summiteers returned safely to their base camp, the ministry said.

The three who managed to scale the peak were 33-year old group leader Park Young-Seok, president of a travel agency in Seoul; Kim Hun-Sang a philosophy student from Seoul who celebrated his 28th birthday at the peak on April 27 and Han Wuang-Yong, 30, a member of Park's travel agency.
They gained the summit with their Nepalese Sherpa, Kaji.
